extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in photography, documentary film, and art criticism
extracted.subtask_description: A critical review of Wim Wenders' documentary Salt of the Earth and Sebastião Salgado's photographic practice, discussing aesthetic, ethical and documentary dimensions of photographic work and its presentation. The page evaluates the film’s composition, the photographer’s methods, and controversies around aestheticizing suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and aesthetic treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado is praised for 'finding the “grace” and “beauty” in the twisted forms of his anguished subjects' and for outstanding composition; composition, exposure and depth of field are described as 'the basic skills of the craft.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive guidance: use careful compositional arrangement and balance of light and dark to emphasise dignity and meaning (the review defends Salgado’s compositional care). Anti-pattern: over-attention to beauty that aestheticises suffering (Ingrid Sischy’s criticism that beautification of tragedy can anaesthetize viewers). Examples: Workers, Serra Pelada images; technical notes: crisp, high-definition images on wide screen amplify compositional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy, immersion and relationship with subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The picture's quality depends on 'the relationship that you have with the people you photograph' — Salgado 'spends some considerable time living with or accompanying those he photographs' rather than shooting quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: invest time, live with subjects, cultivate empathy and understanding to capture essence of the moment. Anti-pattern: rapid, superficial shooting ('shoot quickly and leave') which risks shallow or insulting portrayals. Example: Salgado’s long projects (Other Americas, Sahel, Migrations) and Julian’s observation about his father’s long absences while working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait power and subject agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A portrait's strength is that 'in a split second we understand a little of the life of the person photographed. The eyes speak volumes' and 'when you do a portrait, is not you alone who takes the picture. The person offers the photo.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: aim for moments that reveal expression and life; allow subject participation/agency. Scoring note: portraits that convey interior life (through eyes, expression, posture) score highly. Anti-pattern: portraits that objectify or reduce subject to mere spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context, framing and 'something behind' the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography must have 'something behind' the subject: 'There’s nothing behind. Nothing to frame the photo, to suggest the landscape' — a mere document can lack the elements that make a photograph a true image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: include contextual elements or framing that suggest landscape, history or broader meaning; avoid isolated 'documents' without compositional or contextual anchors. Example: Salgado’s frustrated bear shot (document vs. photo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and willingness to depict suffering directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado’s Sahel images are 'direct and profoundly disturbing depictions of suffering and starvation. Death is constantly present. They are extremely hard to look at.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: do not shy away from confronting scenes when truthful depiction is necessary. Scoring considers the courage and honesty of representation. Anti-pattern: sanitizing or diluting the reality of suffering for comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical awareness about aestheticising suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism (Ingrid Sischy, Susan Sontag) argues that 'beautification of tragedy results in pictures that ultimately reinforce our passivity' and that 'making suffering loom larger... may spur people to feel they ought to “care” more' but may also 'invite them to feel that the sufferings ... are too vast ... to be changed by any local, political intervention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: be conscious of the ethical risk that beauty or spectacle can anaesthetize viewers or depoliticize localized action; balance aesthetic power with contextualization, political clarity, and calls to action. Anti-pattern: producing spectacularly composed images that strip agency from subjects or obscure causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic coherence and long-term project planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado’s major works (Other Americas, Workers, Migrations, Genesis) are 'meticulously' researched and planned long-term projects (e.g., Workers travelled to 26 countries; Migrations spanned seven years and 35 countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: structure work as coherent, researched projects with a clear thematic aim and long-term commitment. Scoring: projects showing sustained focus, planning, and consistent thematic framing score highly. Anti-pattern: ad hoc, unfocused series without research or scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing systemic connections and political economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado’s photographs 'reveal how almost everything that happens on earth is somehow connected' — showing links between inequality, mechanization, environmental destruction, wars, intolerance and migration; Workers 'begins to reveal an image of the operation of global capital.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: aim to make systemic, structural connections visible in images and sequencing; contextualize individual suffering within broader economic and political systems. Scoring: works that successfully show interconnections receive higher evaluative weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and exhibition quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'showcases Salgado’s staggering photography in the best way possible' — 'crisp, high definition images on the wide screen' emphasize his stature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: use high-quality reproduction/display (HD, large format, careful printing/exhibition) to preserve tonal range and detail; poor presentation can diminish impact. Scoring note: technical presentation is part of evaluative criteria for photographic work shown in film or galleries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of praise and critique in documentary biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Some may argue the documentary has 'not produced a fully-rounded portrait of their subject – skirting controversies that have surrounded his work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: for documentary portraits, include major controversies and critical perspectives to produce a balanced, rounded portrait. Anti-pattern: omitting substantive criticisms or counter-views, resulting in hagiography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity of subjects and non-insulting portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer argues Salgado’s pictures are not 'insulting to the people being portrayed' and that his photographs 'bestow dignity and affirm the enduring spirit of working women and men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: composition and editorial choices should aim to confer dignity, emphasize agency and resilience; avoid imagery that humiliates or reduces subjects to spectacle. Example: Workers collection as a tribute to human endeavour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical craft: composition, exposure, depth of field
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical mastery (composition, exposure and depth of field) are cited as 'the basic skills of the craft.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: evaluate technical execution — sharpness, exposure control, tonal range, depth-of-field choices — as foundational to photographic quality. Anti-pattern: technical sloppiness masked by subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and deliberation over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike many photo-journalists, Salgado 'does not shoot quickly, and leave' — he takes time to live with subjects and work slowly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: value patience, repeated visits, and slow work processes in evaluating documentary photography. Quick turnaround reportage may be necessary in some contexts but is distinct from sustained documentary practice; scoring should reflect intended mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of subject matter: documenting destruction vs. celebrating the pristine
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado and Lélia initially planned to 'denounce the destruction of forests and the pollution of the oceans' but decided instead to 'do a different project – a tribute to the planet' focusing on places that remain pristine (Genesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: explicitly define project intent (expose destruction, advocate restoration, celebrate what remains) and evaluate success against that stated purpose. Anti-pattern: incoherent aims or switching purposes without clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and showing common humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado wanted to show that 'even the most isolated group of people are the same as we are' and notes similarities across peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: evaluate whether images communicate shared humanity and relatable human experience across cultural divides without erasing difference. Scoring: images that foster understanding and empathy across contexts are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact beyond images: projects with restorative outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Salgado’s Instituto Terra reforestation project (2.5 million trees, restored streams, national park) is presented as a model that 'others can follow' and as an outcome beyond photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: consider real-world impact or follow-through (environmental restoration, advocacy outcomes) as part of the larger assessment of a photographer’s practice. Anti-pattern: purely aesthetic projects with no engagement or practical outcomes when such engagement is central to stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual 'way of seeing' shaped by personal history
rubrics_metrics.description: Each photographer 'forms their own way of seeing according to their history' — Salgado’s political economy background informed his projects and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: assess the coherence between a photographer’s background, stated concerns and the visual language of their work; credit distinctive vision that arises from lived experience and knowledge.
